trigger_condition: CAP-6 asserts the canonical fixture produces 'PF ₹1,800.00, TDS ₹0.00, net ₹22,230.77 exactly as tabled', but the fixture's expected-numbers table says PF ₹2,400.00 and net ₹21,630.77 — the SPEC numbers are exactly 12% × the obsolete ₹15,000 ceiling (1,800) and 24,230.77 − 1,800 − 200 (22,230.77), written before the ₹25,000 ceiling raise and never refreshed.
guard_snippet: Replace with: 'The canonical fixture (PF on, PT ₹200) produces PF ₹2,400.00, TDS ₹0.00, net ₹21,630.77 exactly as tabled' — or use the pointer pattern (CAP-3's) to the fixture table. Every SPEC sentence citing fixture numbers must be re-checked against the fixture after any oracle edit.
potential_consequence: A story implementing CAP-6 against the SPEC text writes tests that pass against ₹1,800/₹22,230.77, and the QA fixture oracle (2,400/21,630.77) then fails — a spec-vs-oracle fork of exactly the kind the fixture exists to prevent.

location: canonical-fixture.md Variant E, last sentence vs CAP-6 intent and fixture statutory-notes bullet 3
trigger_condition: Variant E states 'a joiner with period basic > ₹25,000 who was never an EPF member is excluded (opt-in via Para 26(6) declaration)', while CAP-6 and the fixture's own statutory-notes block say the opposite is the product default: new joiners are enrolled, cannot claim exclusion; exclusion exists only as an explicit admin configuration.
guard_snippet: Rewrite E's sentence: 'Excluded joiners are a config path, never the default: by default this joiner (period basic > ₹25,000, never an EPF member) is enrolled; an admin may mark them excluded via the admin configuration carrying the EPFO-flux warning; anyone ever an EPF member is covered at any wage.'
potential_consequence: An implementer of the variant-E leg silently defaults above-ceiling joiners to exclusion — the contested EPFO reading the product says it overrides — breaking the CAP-6 enrollment-default acceptance.

location: SPEC.md Run arithmetic vs CAP-5 intent/success
trigger_condition: CAP-5 requires an owner-corrected `half_day` day-status to count as 0.5 LOP day, but the run arithmetic defines LOP-equivalent only from 'approved unpaid-typed leaves … plus day-status `absent` days with no approved leave' — `half_day` is not in the formula, so the engine computes 0 LOP where CAP-5 expects half a day's deduction.
guard_snippet: Extend the run-arithmetic clause: 'LOP-equivalent days = approved unpaid-typed leaves (half-day 0.5) plus day-status `absent` days with no approved leave plus day-status `half_day` days with no paid leave covering that half (0.5 each)' — or re-route CAP-5's acceptance through an unpaid leave part.
potential_consequence: Direct contradiction between the single formula and a named acceptance: the CAP-5 test cannot pass without violating the run-arithmetic test, and one gets quietly weakened at implementation time.

location: SPEC.md Run arithmetic (payable window) vs CAP-8 / fixture G
trigger_condition: The run arithmetic defines the payable window as 'employment window ∩ run month', but CAP-8's cut-off regime says post-cut-off days 'count in month M+1's run as prior-period days' — the formula has no concept of prior-period days. E.g. an employee joining Oct 28 after the cut-off: is the 4-day stub paid in October's run under the window formula, or deferred to November? Under either reading one clause is broken.
guard_snippet: Add one sentence to the run arithmetic: 'Prior-period days (month-M dates after the cut-off) extend the M+1 run's employment window; payable days = employment window ∩ (run month + prior-period days), capped at the divisor' — plus a fixture answer for the joins-just-before-month-end case.
potential_consequence: Joiners/exits near month boundaries are paid under two implementer-chosen readings; the fixture's min(31,26) row validates only the pure calendar-month reading, so a 'prior-period window' implementation passes the fixture yet pays stub months inconsistently.

location: SPEC.md Run arithmetic ('leave spanning months splits per-date by run month'; 'counted only inside the employment window') vs CAP-8 ('a leave on the 27th appears in the next month's run')
trigger_condition: A leave dated Oct 27 must not produce LOP in October's run (post-cut-off, belongs to M+1), but the split rule assigns it to October, and the LOP window rule forbids November's run from deducting an October date — three clauses give no consistent home for the leave.
guard_snippet: Define the LOP window as the same effective run period as the payable window (run month + trailing prior-period days per the cut-off) and replace the per-calendar-month splitting sentence with per-date assignment to the run that owns the date under the cut-off.
potential_consequence: Fixture G's acceptance is unimplementable as written; whichever clause an implementer drops, the employee is either over-deducted in October or never LOP'd — a silent money bug the fixture cannot catch because it tests one direction.

location: SPEC.md CAP-8 (intent 'valid 1–7', success 'on/after the 7th rejected') vs Legal ('payable before the 7th')
trigger_condition: The 7th as pay date is simultaneously valid (intent range 1–7), invalid (success rejects 'on/after the 7th'), and disputed by the legal line — the digest quotes CoW s.17(1) as 'before expiry of the 7th day', which admits the 7th, while the SPEC's Legal bullet writes 'before the 7th', which excludes it.
guard_snippet: Pick one and make all three sites agree, e.g. 'pay date valid 1–7 (CoW s.17(1): payable before expiry of the 7th day of the succeeding month); a pay date after the 7th is rejected with the CoW reason' — delete 'on/after'.
potential_consequence: A tester cannot assert the boundary value; an implementation rejecting the 7th fails a test written from the intent, and one accepting it fails a test written from the success clause — legal exposure either way.

location: SPEC.md CAP-1/CAP-2 vs CAP-6 and CAP-7 (basic component)
trigger_condition: PF is computed on '12% of the basic wages payable' and Form V requires 'wage-rate break-up (basic / DA / allowances)', but no capability designates a component as 'basic' — CAP-1 lets the admin build any component library ('Salary' + 'Travel' qualifies); a structure with no basic component leaves the PF base and Form V fields undefined.
guard_snippet: Add to CAP-1 or CAP-2: 'Exactly one component in the library is designated the basic component (PF base and Form V basic/DA line); a structure without a designated basic is rejected for PF-covered employees / listed not_configured in that case.'
potential_consequence: Run computes PF on an empty/zero base, or the implementer invents a heuristic (first component? name match?) the contract never names — non-statutory PF numbers and unrenderable Form V slips for legal-looking component sets.

trigger_condition: CAP-6 offers CTC as a percentage-head basis, but nothing defines, captures, or computes CTC — CTC is annual, includes the employer PF share, and no CTC field exists in CAP-13 or anywhere else; the fixture never tests a CTC-based head.
guard_snippet: Either drop CTC from the basis list ('flat amount or percentage with basis basic | gross') or define it ('CTC per period = period gross + employer PF share; computed at run time') — and add one fixture row exercising the chosen definition.
potential_consequence: An implementer invents a CTC definition silently (gross × 12? gross + employer PF + gratuity?); every CTC-based head deducts wrong amounts with no oracle to catch it.

location: SPEC.md CAP-6 ('anyone ever previously an EPF member is always covered') vs CAP-13 field set
trigger_condition: Coverage behavior turns on 'was ever an EPF member' and first-coverage grandfathering, but CAP-13 captures no data that determines either — no UAN-presence rule, no first-coverage date, no pre-coverage marker — so the run cannot decide which regime an employee is in.
guard_snippet: State the derivation: 'An employee is ever-member if UAN or PF account number is populated (CAP-13 fields); the first-coverage month is saved when the tenant switches PF-covered on; employees whose join date precedes it are first-coverage existing employees' — or add a per-employee coverage-status field to CAP-13.
potential_consequence: Coverage decisions (who gets PF deducted, who is auto-enrolled above ceiling) are made on undefined inputs; the judicial-line default CAP-6 promises cannot be tested.

location: SPEC.md CAP-2 success + Assumptions ('mid-month-dated revision takes effect from the next run') vs CAP-2 ('revision effective from month M makes M's run use the new structure')
trigger_condition: Admin saves a revision effective 2026-10-15 on Oct 14 and runs October for the first time on Oct 20: 'effective from month M' says October pays the new structure; 'takes effect from the next run' (whole-month rule, meant to defer to November) says the same thing because the next run IS October's — both readings give opposite October results across the not-yet-run vs already-run cases, and the fixture answers only the already-run case (F).
guard_snippet: State the rule per month, not per run: 'A revision effective on any date of month M applies to month M's run only if that run has not yet executed; if M already ran (unlocked), it applies from M+1 — never half-month apportionment either way' — pin with one fixture sentence.
potential_consequence: An October run after a same-month revision either pays the old or the new structure depending on the reader; re-runs of unlocked months silently recompute to a structure the admin believed was history.

location: SPEC.md CAP-4 ('switching the setting affects the next run only') vs Legal ('the LOP divisor [is] effective-dated configuration') and Success signal
trigger_condition: October ran (unlocked); admin flips the divisor to calendar-days; October is re-run — effective-dated config implies the re-run uses the divisor in effect for October (old), 'affects the next run' implies the re-run recomputes with the new convention; nothing states the effective date a policy switch carries (switch date? month start?).
guard_snippet: Declare: 'Non-statutory policy settings (divisor, cut-off, pay date) are timestamped config: a change applies to runs of months that end after the switch date; an unlocked prior month re-runs on the values in effect for that month' — or drop 'effective-dated' from the divisor and accept re-run drift.
potential_consequence: Post-switch re-runs of unlocked months either keep or rewrite history depending on the implementer's reading; already-previewed payslips change or don't with no contract deciding which.

location: SPEC.md CAP-9 ('deduction-head edits affecting the month' rejected with 409) vs CAP-6 (admin heads have no effective dating)
trigger_condition: Statutory values are effective-dated so locked months are safe, but admin-defined deduction heads have no effective-date concept — after October locks, editing the PT head from ₹200 to ₹300 (for November) either 'affects' locked October (409 — and then heads can never be edited once any month is locked) or does not (block's scope undefined); no clause defines 'affecting the month'.
guard_snippet: Either give admin heads the same effective-dated rows as statutory values ('a head edit is a new row effective from the next run; locked months keep stored values, no edit is ever blocked') or define the block precisely: 'a head edit is 409 only if it would change a locked month's snapshotted deduction lines'.
potential_consequence: Deduction heads are frozen forever after the first lock (config dead-end), or the 409 test is written so loosely that legitimate future-facing edits get rejected — CAP-9's acceptance cannot be satisfied deterministically.

trigger_condition: The admin overrides October's TDS to ₹12,000 behind the acknowledgment (variant D); nothing defines whether the override persists into November (silently re-applied without a fresh acknowledgment?), evaporates on recompute, or is month-scoped and must be re-entered and re-acknowledged monthly.
guard_snippet: Add to CAP-6: 'An override is scoped to one employee and one salary period; later periods recompute normally; an override survives unlocked re-runs of its period and is immutable after lock (409).'
potential_consequence: Either the employee is silently over-deducted every following month by a sticky override nobody re-approved, or the accepted override vanishes on the next run and November's payslip diverges from what was confirmed.

location: SPEC.md CAP-6 intent (TDS projection and spread) vs canonical-fixture base TDS row and TDS statutory note
trigger_condition: The TDS projection basis is never stated as a rule — the fixture computes 28,000 × 12 − 75,000 (annualising the monthly structure, not the post-LOP period gross), and 'spread over the remaining months of the financial year' never says whether the run month counts (Oct → 6 or 7 remaining) or whether a mid-FY re-spread claws back under-deduction in later months; every TDS number in the oracle is ₹0.00, so no test pins either parameter.
guard_snippet: State both rule lines in the run arithmetic (or the fixture): 'Projection basis = current monthly structure × 12; spread = remaining months of the FY including the run month; a mid-FY revision re-estimates and re-spreads prospectively' — then add one TDS-positive fixture row that exercises them.
potential_consequence: The most complex computation in the spec is unfalsifiable from its own oracle; two implementations with different projection bases and spread windows both pass every acceptance, and for a ₹50,000/month late-joiner the monthly TDS differs by hundreds of rupees with a catch-up spike the cap may then clamp.

location: SPEC.md CAP-10 ('off-cycle earnings join the wage-period gross for statutory computation') vs CAP-6 (PF on 'basic wages payable') and fixture G
trigger_condition: Fixture G's ₹5,000 bonus makes period gross 29,230.77 — if off-cycle earnings enter the PF base, PF jumps to 12% × min(29,230.77, 25,000) = 3,000; if not, it stays 2,400. 'Join the wage-period gross for statutory computation' does not say which heads (PF? TDS projection?) consume them; the EPF Act excludes bonus from basic wages; fixture G asserts only gross/net, never PF post-bonus.
guard_snippet: Enumerate per head in CAP-10: 'Off-cycle earnings count in the 50%-cap basis and the TDS projection always; they enter the PF base only when the admin tags the line type as wage (arrear/correction), never when tagged bonus' — and add the PF row to fixture G.
potential_consequence: Bonus-inflated PF deductions (statutorily contestable) or under-deducted PF on wage arrears; the payslip disagrees with what the employer must actually remit and no test catches it.

location: SPEC.md CAP-6 (excess-recovery line) and Run arithmetic vs variant D
trigger_condition: Variant D's excess ₹2,969.23 is 'raised as a recovery line on the next run's payslip', but the contract never says whether a recovery line itself counts toward the 50% cap or the PF/TDS base — if it counts toward deductions, an employee already at the cap has the recovery clamped too, minting a new excess and a perpetual clamp-recovery spiral with no terminator.
guard_snippet: Add: 'A recovery line is subject to the same 50% cap check; if the next period's clamp again exceeds the cap, the remaining excess rolls forward as a new recovery line — the run summary shows the outstanding balance' — or exempt it and say so.
potential_consequence: Unbounded chase: each run recovers nothing (clamped at cap), each run generates new excess, the payslip never reconciles and the run summary accumulates a growing un-recoverable debt nobody specified how to clear.

location: SPEC.md CAP-3 ('run months before the company's first payroll month … are rejected')
trigger_condition: 'The company's first payroll month' is defined nowhere in SPEC or fixture — is it the earliest employee join month, the month the tenant enabled payroll, or the earliest backfilled membership created_at (CAP-13's backfill default would push it years into the past for existing tenants)?
guard_snippet: Define it once: 'The first payroll month is the earliest employee join month among ever-active memberships, or the month the tenant first completed payroll setup — computed from config, not created_at backfill defaults' (or a simpler explicit tenant config set on first enable).
potential_consequence: With created_at-derived backfill join dates the rejection rule guards nothing; with a different reading, legitimate first runs are 400-rejected — the CAP-3 rejection acceptance is untestable as written.

location: SPEC.md CAP-3 ('run months … beyond the current cut-off are rejected')
trigger_condition: The contract defines the latest runnable month but not the earliest runnable date — nothing says a month can be run only after its own cut-off day. An October run on Oct 12 (cut-off 25) is allowed as written, yet absences on Oct 13–25 are neither counted in October (run already executed) nor eligible for November (before the cut-off), so they LOP nowhere.
guard_snippet: Add to CAP-8 or CAP-3: 'Month M's run may execute only on or after M's cut-off day; earlier attempts are rejected with the cut-off reason' — or state that a pre-cut-off run treats the remaining days as prior-period days of M+1.
potential_consequence: An eager admin running mid-month creates a permanent un-LOP'd gap: unpaid absences in the run-to-cutoff window are paid in full and never deducted in any month — a silent overpayment the fixture never covers.

location: SPEC.md CAP-7 ('slip number unique per tenant per salary period'; 'regeneration issues a new slip number') vs Constraints ('gap-free' counter) and CAP-3 ('one payslip per employee')
trigger_condition: Re-running the unlocked month twice leaves dead slip numbers — 'gap-free' allocation holds but the set of live slips gaps, and the contract never says whether the superseded payslip row is deleted ('one payslip per employee') or versioned (which would collide with 'unique per tenant per salary period' unless the unique key changes).
guard_snippet: Declare both semantics: 'Superseded payslip rows are destroyed and replaced (one live row per employee-period; the prior presigned URL is invalidated); slip numbers are allocated gap-free but the live set may gap after regeneration — no uniqueness or consecutiveness test over live rows'.
potential_consequence: Tests written from 'gap-free' + 'unique' fail on any re-run with prior periods, or an implementer version-rows payslips and accidentally violates the uniqueness the spec demands; superseded PDF URLs may stay live, leaking stale numbers.

location: SPEC.md CAP-3 ('owners/admins and removed members are excluded unless explicitly configured in')
trigger_condition: The clause grants an exception 'unless explicitly configured in' but no capability, config, or mechanism anywhere in the contract can include an owner/admin in a run — CAP-1..13 define no such switch, so 'explicitly configured in' refers to a feature that does not exist.
guard_snippet: Either delete the clause ('owners/admins and removed members are excluded in v1, no configuration path') or specify the one mechanism intended (e.g. 'an owner who also holds an active technician membership is paid via the standard eligibility rules').
potential_consequence: A story implements an inclusion config nobody specified (invented contract surface, scope creep past the lean decree), or the exclusion is silently absolute with testers finding no defined behavior for the working-owner case.

location: SPEC.md Legal and CAP-7 (Form V, rule 52, CoW (Central) Rules 2026, Gazette 8 May 2026) vs statutory-gapcheck-r3-1.md Q2
trigger_condition: The kernel's complete-contract header declares the statutory digest the operative legal basis — but that digest records the wage-slip form as NOT FOUND ('operative slip form not retrieved', field list 'LEAD, not finding', recommends per-state field sets), so CAP-7's load-bearing Form V/rule-52 citation has no supporting line in the declared companion set.
guard_snippet: Fold the Form V verification into the contract: add the verification digest that established Form V/rule 52 (the four statutory deep-checks) to the companions list or as a digest in the research run folder — so the 'authoritative for tests' field set is traceable to a legal-basis source inside the contract.
potential_consequence: The most statutory-facing surface (the payslip every test asserts against) rests on a citation the contract's own designated legal-basis document could not retrieve; if the form reference is off by rule number or field set, CAP-7's acceptance and generated PDF freeze on a wrong template.

location: canonical-fixture.md PF rows and statutory notes (₹25,000 ceiling, S.O. 5109(E)) vs research.md and statutory-gapcheck-r3-1.md Q8
trigger_condition: Every PF number in the test oracle rides on the wage-ceiling raise, but the declared companions don't carry it — research.md states ₹15,000 unchanged since 2014, the statutory digest records the ceiling as unverified and never mentions a raise — so the ₹25,000/S.O. 5109(E)/17-Sep-2026 claim exists only in fixture prose and the SPEC's Open Questions, outside the declared legal-basis companion set; the stale CAP-6 acceptance shows this gap already bit one clause.
guard_snippet: Add the ceiling-raise verification (S.O. 5109(E) primary text / EPFO FAQ / KPMG 2026-249) as a digest under the statutory companion, and add a fixture line naming the config rows the test seeds (two effective-dated ceiling rows: ₹15,000 pre-2026-09-17, ₹25,000 from) so the oracle's ceiling is data, not prose.
potential_consequence: The contract is internally at war over the ceiling (research ₹15,000, fixture ₹25,000, CAP-6's stale numbers arguably ₹15,000); an implementer trusting any of the three produces results that disagree, and the two-value config has no ensurable test data.

location: SPEC.md CAP-7 / canonical-fixture.md Payslip day-count fields line
trigger_condition: The fixture's day-count buckets do not reconcile — payable 26 = paid 22.5 + LOP 3.5, but adding paid-typed leave 2 and weekly offs 4 overshoots a 31-day month (the divisor cap discards days); the fixture header says 'Tests import these rows verbatim' while a parenthetical simultaneously demotes them to story-level presentation — contradictory instructions; and no definition of Form V 'paid days / days worked' resolves it.
guard_snippet: Mark the money rows 'assertions core' and the day-count rows 'presentation pending story-level definition' with one reconciliation rule: 'paid days = payable − LOP-equivalent (22.5); days worked counts present days with half_day as 0.5; the divisor cap discards excess calendar days and the buckets are not required to sum to calendar days' — then drop 'import these rows verbatim' or scope it.
potential_consequence: A tester writes contradictions as assertions (buckets must sum to 31 → false fail), or skips the day-count rows and CoW Form V's mandated attendance fields ship undefined.

location: SPEC.md CAP-7 field set / Non-goals (ESI absent)
trigger_condition: Form V requires an ESI deduction line and CoW s.18(2) permits ESI contributions as deductions, but no clause says what produces the ESI amount in v1 — unlike PF (auto-computed), TDS (estimated), PT (admin head), ESI is neither computed, declared an admin-head responsibility, nor listed in Non-goals. Trigger: a 10-employee tenant, worker gross ₹12,000/month (inside the ESI wage band), run shows ESI 0.00/blank with no admin pathway having produced it.
guard_snippet: One line in Non-goals (or CAP-6): 'No ESI computation/threshold logic in v1; admins model ESI (0.75%) as a per-employee percentage head if applicable; the Form V ESI line renders the computed head value or 0.00' — deciding by decree, like PT/LWF, rather than by silence.
potential_consequence: An implementer either silently skips ESI (non-compliant slips for covered employees, with no documented divergence unlike the recorded F&F one) or over-builds an ESI engine past the lean decree — 'silent ESI' is exactly the 'never a silent ₹0' failure mode CAP-3 bans for structures.

trigger_condition: Revision effective-dated into an already-run unlocked month; the whole-month rule says 'next run'
guard_snippet: Pin re-run semantics: a re-run reads the structure effective for that run month (day 1), not the save-time 'next run'
potential_consequence: Backdated revision skipped by its own month or applied to the wrong month

trigger_condition: 'Owners/removed members excluded unless explicitly configured in' — the configuring mechanism is undefined
guard_snippet: Remove the clause or name the capability/config row that opts a member into payroll runs
potential_consequence: Unowned escape hatch; exclusion implemented divergently per story or not at all

trigger_condition: Employee has an effective structure but join date after run month (or exit before it)
guard_snippet: Run skips any employee whose employment window ∩ run month is empty, flagged in the run summary
potential_consequence: Zero- or negative-day ₹0 payslip issued, violating the never-silent-₹0 invariant

trigger_condition: 'Before the company's first payroll month' — nothing defines or configures that month
guard_snippet: Define first payroll month = payroll-enabled date / first completed run, stored on payroll config
potential_consequence: Rejection boundary arbitrary; backpay months blocked or allowed inconsistently

trigger_condition: TDS spread over 'remaining months of the financial year' — run month inclusive/exclusive unpinned
guard_snippet: Pin denominator: FY months run-month-through-March inclusive; leaver's final month deducts full remaining tax
potential_consequence: Same annual tax divided by 5 vs 6; leaver final-pay TDS undefined or zero

trigger_condition: Annual salary projection for a prorated month (mid-month join/exit) — basis undefined
guard_snippet: Pin: project structure amount × 12 (not period earnings), with a fixture row for a prorated month
potential_consequence: Slab/rebate misestimated for partial months; wrong TDS propagates across remaining months

trigger_condition: Mid-FY joiner — 'annual salary income' projected ×12 vs employment months in FY
guard_snippet: Pin projection horizon: structure × months employed within the FY, with a fixture row
potential_consequence: TDS over-deducted for mid-FY joiners; s.157 rebate wrongly denied

trigger_condition: Percentage deduction head with basis CTC — CTC is never defined anywhere
guard_snippet: Define basis map (CTC = gross + employer PF share) or drop CTC from the basis list
potential_consequence: Un-implementable basis; same head computes differently across stories

trigger_condition: Percentage head on basic under LOP — period (LOP-reduced) basic vs structure basic unpinned
guard_snippet: Pin basis-basic = basic wages payable for the period (mirroring the PF base) with a fixture row
potential_consequence: Same head over- or under-deducts depending on the implementer's reading

trigger_condition: Company PF-covered switch off, employee is a prior EPF member (UAN present)
guard_snippet: State precedence: ever-member flag forces PF computation regardless of the company switch
potential_consequence: Statutorily covered employee processed with zero PF; chronic under-deduction

trigger_condition: Cap-excess recovery line due on the next run; employee exits or is skipped that month
guard_snippet: Recovery carries into the final/exit payslip; recovery lines excluded from next month's cap and bases
potential_consequence: Excess never recovered, or recovery line itself re-clamped causing cascading recovery

trigger_condition: Admin override applied, then the unlocked month re-runs — persisted or recomputed?
guard_snippet: Pin: overrides are effective-dated config rows re-applied on re-run until explicitly removed
potential_consequence: Re-run silently wipes or double-applies an employer-acknowledged override

trigger_condition: Payslip template lists an ESI deduction field but no CAP computes or scopes ESI
guard_snippet: Add to Non-goals: ESI auto-computation; ESI appears only via admin-defined deduction head
potential_consequence: ESI line silently always ₹0.00, or a story invents unreviewed ESI computation

trigger_condition: Prior-period days (post-cut-off, CAP-8:55) sit outside the 'window ∩ run month' payable formula
guard_snippet: Extend the invariant: payable window = employment dates ∩ (run month ∪ prior-period dates); add a leaver fixture row
potential_consequence: Leaver exiting after cut-off has final days paid with attendance never evaluated by any run

trigger_condition: Employment window contains not_tracked days (enrolment gap or attendance ended before exit)
guard_snippet: Define not_tracked days inside the window as paid-by-default plus a run-summary flag (or LOP), explicitly
potential_consequence: Gap days silently full-paid or miscounted as absent-LOP; only fully-unenrolled employees are flagged

trigger_condition: Approved unpaid half-day leave, but employee absent (no check-in) on the other half
guard_snippet: If a half_day_leave day carries zero daysWorked credit, add 0.5 absent-side LOP-equivalent
potential_consequence: Half-day absence escapes LOP; 0.5 day under-deducted per occurrence

trigger_condition: Owner override (present/absent/half_day) applied to a day holding an approved leave
guard_snippet: Pin precedence: latest override status replaces that day's leave-derived LOP (or state the reverse)
potential_consequence: Day paid per override yet still LOP-deducted per leave, or the reverse

trigger_condition: Pay date set to the 7th — intent says 'valid 1–7', success rejects on/after the 7th
guard_snippet: Align both lines: valid 1–6 under CoW 'before the 7th', or admit the 7th in both
potential_consequence: A valid config rejected (or a non-compliant date accepted) depending on which line implements

trigger_condition: Month M locked; corrections/leave approvals target M's post-cut-off days consumed by M+1's run
guard_snippet: Lock freezes pre-cut-off dates only; the 26th–end stays editable until M+1's run consumes them
potential_consequence: M+1 run consumes attendance frozen mid-approval, or valid corrections get permanent 409

trigger_condition: Locking a payroll month that has never run
guard_snippet: Require a completed run before lock (409 otherwise), or define an explicit empty-lock flow
potential_consequence: Month locked unrun: re-run rejected forever, employees never paid

trigger_condition: checkout_missing day corrected to absent after its month is locked (overpay discovered)
guard_snippet: Permit a negative off-cycle 'recovery' line (admin-acknowledged) in the next unlocked month
potential_consequence: Overpayment irrecoverable: off-cycle is defined as an earning only

trigger_condition: Staged off-cycle earning for a skipped employee, or a month locked without ever running
guard_snippet: Reject off-cycle for never-structured employees; list orphaned staged lines in lock confirmation and run summary
potential_consequence: Earned money silently vanishes or blocks the lock; owed amounts never surface

trigger_condition: Exit date earlier than join date captured — no validation defined in CAP-13
guard_snippet: CAP-13 acceptance: exit_date ≥ join_date enforced at save; inverted rows rejected with error
potential_consequence: Empty/inverted window reaches the run; negative-day arithmetic silently floored

trigger_condition: Formula divides by a zero-valued operand; component amounts may be zero/negative
guard_snippet: Save-time validation: reject ÷ by zero-amount operand; reject negative component amounts
potential_consequence: Infinity/NaN wage lines at run time, or negative salary structures accepted

trigger_condition: Run requested on the cut-off day itself — 'beyond the current cut-off' boundary unpinned
guard_snippet: Pin: month M runnable from cut-off day 00:00 tenant tz; attendance inclusive of the cut-off day
potential_consequence: Run on the 25th either rejected or silently excludes the 25th's attendance

trigger_condition: Async run worker dies or hangs — no timeout, failed status, or retry semantics defined
guard_snippet: Define the run status machine incl. a terminal failed state with retry; advisory lock freed on session end
